items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S2813

TITLE OF BILL:
An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to establishing
the North Country power authority, and providing for its powers and
duties

PURPOSE OF BILL:
To create a public benefit corporation, a political subdivision of the
state, to provide electric power services to designated municipalities
in St. Lawrence and Franklin Counties.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:
Establishes the North Country Power Authority to provide electric power
services to designated municipalities in St. Lawrence and Franklin Coun-
ties, to be governed by a board of directors with overlapping terms,
with enumerated powers to acquire, own, operate and finance facilities
to provide electric power services, to issue bonds of up to 50 years and
notes and other debt obligations of up to 5 years, which securities are
to be general obligations of the authority without any state or munici-
pal liability, permitting sale of surplus power and establishment of
subsidiaries, subjecting the authority to conflict of interest prohibi-
tions, deposit and investment controls, annual auditing and reporting to
state and local officials and the public, and mandating periodic legis-
lative reviews starting in 2050 and discretionary termination through
statute after each such review subject to terms of the authority's secu-
rities, together with attendant provisions for implementing and conduct-
ing its financing and operating responsibilities.

JUSTIFICATION:
Enabling legislation is essential to establish a public power utility to
finance and operate a municipal electric system serving a group of 24
municipalities in St. Lawrence and Franklin Counties, all of which have
endorsed the creation of the authority and the proposed legislation.
These counties in the North Country constitute an area where economic
growth has been lagging for years and one that faces very high rates for
electric services to residential and commercial consumers. The affected
municipalities are committed to securing lower electricity rates, great-
er service reliability, local public control and future emphasis on
energy conservation and sustainability through this new public power
utility, built on a model common in this country.  The public authority
is necessary to provide financing, which would be stand-alone revenue
bonding without any recourse to the state or the municipalities. The act
is replete with good governance provisions, financial discipline meas-
ures, transparency and reporting requirements, and accountability to the
governor, the legislature, the municipalities and the public to be
served.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
S.8257-A - 2008

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediate.
